question: Does Ramapo have a nursing program, and is there an accelerated option for people who already have a bachelor's degree?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers a Bachelor of Science in Nursing (BSN), with generic, accelerated, and RN-to-BSN tracks. [2][3]

Yes—there is an accelerated BSN for people who hold a non-Nursing bachelor’s degree. The program page also says it is for prospective students with a minimum of 60 credits from a regionally-accredited institution. [1] It is a full-time, daytime, in-person program. [1]

For application requirements and instructions, Admissions links to https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-requirements/ and https://www.ramapo.edu/nursing/accelerated-bsn/application-instructions/. [5] Accelerated BSN applicants are required to have a 3.0 cumulative grade point average or above. [6]

Admissions: admissions@ramapo.edu; (201) 684-7300.

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURA) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURS) [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/undergraduate/transfer/admission-requirements/)

question: how many credits do you need to graduate with a bachelors at ramapo
answer:
A Ramapo bachelor’s degree requires at least 128 credits that count toward graduation; some programs may require more, and program requirements differ. [6][10] [15]

Ramapo-credit residency requirements differ across the pages: sections 5 and 7 say you need at least 48 credits at Ramapo, including your final 32 in residence. Sections 8, 9 and 10 say at least 32 credits at Ramapo; sections 9 and 10 also require your final 32 in residence, while section 9 allows an approved Ramapo study abroad program or experience. The pages differ; check with your adviser about what applies to you. [5][7][8][9][10]

Sources: [5](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [6](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/graduation-commencement/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/) [9](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#undergraduate-residency-requirement1) [10](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#graduation-requirements) [15](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/policies/)

question: My daughter wants to do psychology. What courses would she take freshman year and is there a recommended 4 year plan?
answer:

Freshman year [1]:
Fall (16 credits): INTD 101 - FIRST YEAR SEMINAR; Gen Ed – - SOCIAL SCIENCE INQUIRY; PSYC 101 - INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY; CRWT 102 - CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II.
Spring (16 credits): General Education Requirement (twice); Quantitative Reasoning – (Preferred) MATH 108 - ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS; Category 1 Course: Social and Organizational; PATH 001 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 1.

Recommended four-year plan [1]:
Year 2 fall (16): General Education Requirement; Category 2 Course: Cognition and Perception; Category 3 Course: Developmental*; Free Elective (minor, certificate, or second major requirement); PATH 002 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 2.
Year 2 spring (16): General Education Requirement; PSYC 242 - STATISTICS; Category 4 Course: Sociocultural Perspectives; Free Elective (minor, certificate, or second major requirement); PATH 003 - CAREER PATHWAYS MOD 3.
Year 3 fall (16): General Education Requirement; PSYC 303 - RESEARCH METHODS IN PSYCHOLOGY WI; PSYC 304 - DATA ANALYSIS IN PSYCHOLOGY; Psychology Elective.
Year 3 spring (16): Category 5 Course: Clinical Perspectives; three Free Electives (minor, certificate, or second major requirement).
Year 4 fall (16): Category 6: Brain and Behavior; Category 7: (Fieldwork) WI; two Free Electives (minor, certificate, or second major requirement).
Year 4 spring (16): Category 8 Capstone Seminar WI; three Free Electives (minor, certificate, or second major requirement). Total Credits Required: 128 credits. GPA: 2.0. [1]

question: what are the gen ed requirements at ramapo? like how many credits are general education vs the major
answer:
Ramapo’s General Education curriculum is ten courses: four keystone courses (First Year Seminar, Social Science Inquiry, Critical Reading & Writing 102, and Studies in the Arts & Humanities); one course each in Global Awareness, Historical Perspectives, Scientific Reasoning, and Quantitative Reasoning; and one course in two of the three distribution categories [10]. Critical Reading & Writing 102 and Quantitative Reasoning must be completed within the first 64 credits. At least one distribution course must be offered by a school other than the one housing your major [10].

The curriculum “should not exceed 41 credits”; it is not stated as a fixed 41-credit requirement [6]. One course cannot satisfy two separate General Education competencies, and no more than two Gen Ed courses may also count toward your major [6]. For Fall 2026, the distribution category names differ between pages: section 9 says “Social Systems and Society,” while section 10 says “Systems, Sustainability, & Society” [9][10].

An undergraduate degree consists of General Education, a major, and free electives [12]. Ramapo requires 128 credits overall, but program requirements differ [13]. The pages don’t give a single credit total for your major or an exact Gen Ed-versus-major split; check your program with an adviser [13]. Contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): success@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7441.

Sources: [6](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [9](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/home/comprehensive-academic-plan/resources/) [10](https://www.ramapo.edu/provost/curriculum-and-assessment/) [12](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1) [13](https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/faq/)

question: Is there a 5 year combined bachelors and masters program? Which majors have it?
answer:
Yes. Ramapo offers 4+1 programs to earn a bachelor’s and master’s degree in five years [9]. The catalog lists these 4+1 programs: Accounting, Applied Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Public Policy, and Special Education [3].

The Computer Science 4+1 is designed for students in the Computer Science BS, Data Science BS, and Mathematics BS; students in other disciplines may contact the Graduate Program Director about a 5-year plan [1]. Accounting 4+1 is an option for current Ramapo Accounting majors or minors; other business majors may qualify as well [2]. The listed programs do not establish which undergraduate majors are eligible for every other 4+1 program [3].

To declare a 4+1, contact the graduate program director for enrollment information and guidelines, then use the 4+1 Declaration Form: https://www.ramapo.edu/registrar/wp-content/uploads/sites/7/2026/04/41-Declaration-Form-FILLABLE.pdf [9].

question: Should my kid major in nursing or biology if she wants to be a PA eventually? which one is better at ramapo
answer:
Ramapo’s pages do not say which major is better for becoming a PA or compare PA preparation, so I can’t recommend one based on verified college information. [1][3]

The Biology BS describes a flexible foundation in biology and lets students choose courses reflecting their interests. [1] The generic Nursing BSN is designed for students interested in becoming nurses; students complete general education and science courses before a two-year nursing sequence. [3] The pages describe Nursing preparation for nursing, not PA preparation. [3]

For help deciding, the Center for Student Success says to define the decision; gather information by reading the catalog, attending School events, asking questions and talking with advisors and students; use Cahill Career Development Center computer tests; consider PLACE, talk with upper-level students and professional advisors, and seek a related summer job; focus choices through classes and faculty conversations; then assess costs and risks, and gain co-op or internship experience.
